report: Analysis A3: Pointer Network Use Cases and Applications

1_knowledge_discovery.title: Knowledge Discovery via Non-Obvious Network Traversal
1_knowledge_discovery.current_gap: Agents currently find knowledge via CLAUDE.md instructions or explicit file paths. They miss connections that span 2+ hops across domains.

scenarios.name: Cross-domain serendipity
scenarios.description: An agent working on a stress-test script (SCR-0036) follows shared_tags to KB-0001 (stress test results), which links via builds_on to TEAM-0008 and TEAM-0006. Those team logs reference SOP-015 (testing procedures). The agent discovers testing SOPs it would never have searched for directly.
scenarios.value: Agent discovers established testing procedures instead of inventing its own approach

scenarios.name: Wikipedia bridge pattern
scenarios.description: The network has 114 wikipedia nodes bridging conceptual knowledge to practical tools. An agent researching 'reinforcement learning' (wiki node) can traverse to ML trading scripts and relevant data sources without knowing they exist.
scenarios.value: Conceptual research automatically surfaces practical implementations

scenarios.name: Indirect dependency discovery
scenarios.description: Source SRC-0001 (OpenAlex API, 41 pointers) connects to 7 related sources and SCR-0023. An agent using SCR-0023 can discover all alternative data sources it could swap to if OpenAlex is down.

algorithm.name: serendipity_walk
algorithm.description: BFS traversal that crosses domain boundaries at each hop, collecting nodes with weight >= threshold. Returns paths that touch >= 3 distinct domains.
pseudocode: for ptr in node.pointers where ptr.weight >= min_weight:

2_onboarding.title: Agent Onboarding via Network-as-Map
2_onboarding.current_gap: New agents read CLAUDE.md, then must manually explore directories. The pointer network could provide a structured 'tour' based on task type.

for_coding_tasks.reason: Most-used entry node (16 entries in route log). Links to testing SOPs and scripts.

for_research_tasks.reason: Second-most-used entry (15 entries). Connects to knowledge base and team logs.

for_coordination_tasks.reason: Highly connected coordination SOP (15 entries). Bidirectional with SOP-014 and SOP-015.

for_data_tasks.reason: Highest-connected node in the network (41 pointers). Gateway to all data sources.

onboarding_paths.name: The Grand Tour
onboarding_paths.description: 5-hop path touching all major domains. Gives agent a complete mental model.
onboarding_paths.path: SOP-011 (coordination) -> SOP-015 (testing) -> SCR-0036 (stress-test script) -> KB-0001 (stress test knowledge) -> TEAM-0001 (team log) -> SRC-0001 (data sources)

onboarding_paths.name: Quick Orient
onboarding_paths.description: 3-hop path for agents that need to start working immediately.
onboarding_paths.path: SOP-028 (pointer network SOP) -> SOP-029 (route tracking) -> relevant SOP for task type

implementation.suggestion: Add a 'recommend --task onboarding --entry SOP-028' mode to route_tracker.py that returns a curated tour path based on the agent's declared task type.

3_impact_analysis.title: Change Impact Traversal Algorithm
3_impact_analysis.current_gap: When a script or SOP changes, there is no automated way to find what depends on it. The pointer network encodes these dependencies via explicit_reference and builds_on edges.

algorithm.name: impact_cascade
algorithm.description: Given a changed node, find all nodes that could be affected by traversing incoming edges (backlinks) and strong outgoing edges.
pseudocode: # Phase 1: Find all nodes pointing TO the changed node (reverse lookup)
# Phase 2: BFS on reverse edges (who depends on this?)
# Only cascade if edge is primary or supporting (strong dependency)
# Phase 3: Forward edges with explicit_reference reason
edge = find_edge_between(node_id, changed_node) or find_edge_between(changed_node, node_id)

severity_rules.breaking: Edge has explicit_reference:builds_on AND weight >= 6 AND strength is primary
severity_rules.needs_review: Edge has explicit_reference AND weight >= 4 OR strength is supporting
severity_rules.informational: Edge is shared_tags only or weight < 4

example_scenario.impact: 12 scripts reference SCR-0001. Changing validation logic could break SCR-0002 (edge cases), SCR-0003 (bulk test), and all stress-test scripts.

3_impact_analysis.reverse_index_note: The current pointer network does not include pre-built reverse indexes. Adding a 'backlinks' field to each node (or building it at load time) would make impact analysis O(1) per lookup instead of O(N) full scan.

4_quality_assurance.title: Network-Based Quality Assurance Checks
4_quality_assurance.current_gap: No automated staleness detection, orphan detection, or reference integrity checking is done against the pointer network itself.

checks.name: stale_knowledge_detection
checks.description: Knowledge entries (KB-*) that have no recent team logs pointing to them may be stale. Cross-reference KB node dates with TEAM node dates.
checks.algorithm: For each KB node: find all TEAM nodes it connects to. If the newest TEAM connection is > 30 days old and no route_log entries reference it, flag as potentially stale.
checks.data_available: Yes - knowledge-base/index.json has dates, teams/ has session dates

checks.name: orphaned_script_detection
checks.description: Scripts with no inbound pointers from SOPs or KB entries are likely orphaned (no procedure references them).
checks.algorithm: Build reverse index. For each SCR-* node, check if any SOP-* or KB-* node points to it. If none do, flag as orphaned.
checks.current_finding: KB-0034 has only 2 pointers — the least connected node in the network. It may be orphaned or incomplete.

checks.name: broken_reference_detection
checks.description: Pointer targets that don't exist as nodes in the network indicate broken references.
checks.algorithm: For each pointer edge, verify ptr.to exists in nodes{}. Report any dangling pointers.
checks.note: The network builder (SCR-0057 likely) should already validate this, but a runtime check catches drift.

checks.name: strength_classification_audit
checks.description: 81.5% of edges (3931/4820) are 'unclassified'. This reduces the utility of strength-based routing.
checks.recommendation: Run a classification pass: edges with explicit_reference reasons should be primary/supporting. Edges with only shared_tags and weight < 3 should be tangential.
checks.impact: Would improve route_tracker.py recommend accuracy by providing strength signals on 3931 currently unclassified edges

checks.name: sop_tool_reference_validation
checks.description: SOPs reference specific scripts and tools. Verify that every tool/script mentioned in an SOP text exists as a node in the pointer network.
checks.algorithm: Parse SOP markdown files for SCR-* and SRC-* references. Cross-check against pointer-network.json nodes.

4_quality_assurance.implementation_suggestion: Create a QA script (e.g., SCR-0058 'pointer-network-qa.py') that runs all five checks and outputs a health report. Could be integrated into validate-storage.py.

5_cross_project_applicability.title: Generalizing the Pointer Network Pattern
5_cross_project_applicability.assessment: The pointer network pattern is highly generalizable. Its core value proposition — making implicit relationships explicit and machine-traversable — applies to any codebase with multiple interrelated artifact types.

what_makes_it_generalizable.explanation: Nodes only need an ID, a domain label, and a list of typed pointers. This fits any artifact: API endpoints, database tables, config files, test suites, documentation pages.
Numeric weights with human-readable reasons (shared_tags, explicit_reference) let both humans and algorithms prioritize edges. This works for any relationship type.
The primary/supporting/related/tangential hierarchy maps naturally to any dependency system: npm packages, microservice dependencies, database foreign keys.
The route_tracker.py pattern of logging traversals and analyzing patterns is applicable to any graph-navigating system. It provides ground truth for optimizing the network.

6_market_research_integration.title: Connecting Financial Analysis Methods to Data Sources via Pointer Network
6_market_research_integration.gap_analysis: Market research methods and picks are NOT currently represented in the pointer network. The 48 data sources (SRC-*) in the network include scientific APIs (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar) but the connection to financial data sources in market-research/methods/ is missing.

connection_strategies.description: Each method category (e.g., nlp-sentiment) should point to data sources that provide the required data type (e.g., news APIs, SEC filing APIs). Edges use shared_tags on data type.
KB entries about quantitative analysis (KB-0003 'Quantitative Stock Analysis with AI') should link to relevant method categories.
When a stock pick is made, the pointer network records which method produced it, enabling performance attribution.

implementation_steps: 1. Add market-research node extraction to the pointer network builder (SCR-0057 or equivalent)
2. Define tag vocabulary overlap between market-research categories and existing SRC-* tags
3. Run network rebuild to generate MR-* nodes and cross-domain edges
4. Validate new edges with a QA pass
5. Update route_tracker.py recommend to handle MR-* entry nodes

value_propositions: An agent doing financial research can start at MR-METHOD-nlp-sentiment and discover all available text data sources, relevant scripts, and prior team knowledge in one traversal
Performance tracking: when a pick succeeds or fails, traverse back to the method and data source to attribute performance
Method gap detection: if a method category has no data source pointers, it indicates missing data infrastructure
Cross-pollination: wiki nodes about financial concepts can bridge to both market research methods AND existing KB entries

highest_impact_use_cases.reason: Directly prevents bugs. When SCR-0001 (validate-storage) changes, the network identifies 12+ affected scripts immediately. Currently this is done manually or not at all.
81.5% of edges are unclassified. Fixing this multiplies the value of all other use cases. Orphan and staleness detection prevents knowledge rot.
The serendipity_walk algorithm could surface connections agents miss. The wikipedia bridge (114 nodes) is a unique asset not being leveraged.

quick_wins: Build reverse index (backlinks) into pointer-network.json — enables O(1) impact analysis
Classify the 3931 unclassified edges using simple rules (explicit_reference -> primary, shared_tags-only with weight < 3 -> tangential)
Add --onboard flag to route_tracker.py recommend for new agent orientation
Create pointer-network-qa.py script for automated health checks

strengths: 310 nodes across 7 domains with 4820 edges — good coverage
Route tracking already operational with 155 logged routes
Hub nodes (SRC-0001 at 41 pointers) provide strong connectivity
Cross-domain edges are abundant (wikipedia->scripts alone has 533)
weaknesses: Market research domain is completely absent from the network
No reverse index / backlinks built into the network structure
KB-0034 is nearly isolated (2 pointers) — potential orphan
No automated QA or staleness detection currently exists
